summary: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He studied at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (BA, under George F. Dales), and became Professor of Anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Scott worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He founded The Asiatic Society and served as Professor of Oriental Languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1802) and the East India Company College (circa 1806–1808).

A religious studies scholar, Jonathan Z. Smith studied at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University. He held posts at Dartmouth College, UC Santa Barbara, the University of Chicago (Dean of the College 1977–1982), and SBL (president 2008).

Jong-Nam Choi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen), also receiving instruction from Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Jongcheol Lee studied at Seoul National University and earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (1994) under Yasunori Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and Academy of Korean Studies (2001).

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA 1994, under Robert E. Buswell Jr.), later becoming Associate Professor at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba specialized in Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied and held multiple academic posts at Ryukoku University (including Professor Emeritus 1970–1989), and directed institutions including the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute and Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies.

Jos Gommans works in history and Indology. He studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University, completing his doctorate under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. He was a fellow at the Dutch Research Council before becoming professor at Leiden.

Linguist Jos. Schrijnen studied at KU Leuven (PhD 1891) and the University of Paris under scholars including Ferdinand de Saussure. He held posts at Utrecht University (1910–1921) and served as Rector and ordinary Professor at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1938).

Josef Baudiš was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (under Josef Zubatý) and Heidelberg University. He held an appointment as Privatdozent at Charles University around 1910 and became Professor at Comenius University in 1924.

Indologist Josef Friedrich Kohl studied at the German University in Prague and the University of Bonn (PhD under Willibald Kirfel). He served as Privatdozent at Bonn (1940) and Prague (1943–1945), and apl. Professor at the University of Würzburg (1957).

Josef Horovitz worked in religious studies and history. Educated at Marburg and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD 1897 under Eduard Sachau), he held professorships at Aligarh Muslim University (1907–1914) and Goethe University Frankfurt (1915), and founded Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Josef Jungmann was a linguist who studied at Charles University in 1795 and later held a post there from around 1815 to 1845.

Josef Kohler specialized in Indology and legal history. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Freiburg, later serving as Professor at the University of Würzburg (1878) and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1888).

Josef Kuckertz worked in Indology and ethnomusicology. He studied at Rheinische Musikschule and the University of Cologne (PhD and habilitation), where he was Professor of Musicology from 1970, before becoming Professor at the Free University of Berlin in 1980.
Josef Maria Abs was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi and held a professorship at the University of Calcutta in 1914.

Josef Markwart worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and linguistics. He studied at Bonn and Tübingen (PhD), and held posts at Tübingen, the National Museum of Ethnology, Leiden University, and Humboldt University of Berlin (Professor from 1912).

Josef Partsch was a historian and legal scholar who studied at the University of Breslau (1900–1904). He held posts at Humboldt University, Göttingen, Geneva, Freiburg (1908–1920), and Bonn (1920–1925).

Josef Schick was a linguist who studied at Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD under Albrecht Weber). He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg University (1893–1896), and the University of Munich as ordinary Professor (1896–1925).

Josef Strzygowski was an art historian who studied at Vienna, Berlin, and Munich (PhD 1885). He held posts at the University of Graz, Åbo Akademi University, and the University of Vienna, where he served as Professor of Art History (1909–1933).
